successors.text: the Avar remnant on the Hungarian plain and the Transylvanian east, taken by Bulgaria 804-806

successors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
successors.text: Pannonia west of the Danube-Tisza line

capitals.name: Khagan's camp on the Pontic steppe (place not named on the pages)
The Khagan's court, 'the Ring' (Hungarian plain; place not named on the pages)

ledger.x: 561: the Avars, who reached Europe in 557-559 from the Caucasus steppe, hold the lower Danube and the Pontic steppe under Khagan Baian.
567: the Avars and Lombards destroy the Gepid kingdom.
568: the Lombards leave Pannonia for Italy and the Avars take it over.
582: the Avars capture Sirmium.
583: the Avars take the Danube cities.
602: the Balkan war of Maurice's reign ends.
615: the Avars take the Balkan interior.
626: the Slavs under Samo break away from the Avars.
June 626: the Avars and Persians besiege Constantinople.
August 626: the siege fails.
627: after Constantinople the Avar hold on the Balkans collapses.
627: the Slavic tribes of the Balkans leave Avar rule.

c. 633: Kubrat's Onogur Bulgars shake off Avar rule. 'Between 630 and 635, Khan Kubrat managed to unite the Onogur Bulgars' and 'quickly managed to overthrow Avar domination'; infobox reign 632-665. 409 cells, all in Old Great Bulgaria's shape of 633.
656: Great Bulgaria widens into Avar land.
656: the Avar claim on the Dniester-Dnieper steppe lapses.

c. 661: part of Samo's former union returns to the Avars. 'With the death of Samo in 658 and Kubrat in 665, some Slavic tribes again came under Avar rule.' 52 cells, 20 of them in Samo's shape of 658; the year is Cliopatria's. c. 680: Asparukh's Bulgars settle north and south of the lower Danube. The Avar land 'was further reduced by the Bulgars around 680'; the Pannonian Avars page has 'The Danube settlement (c. 679-681), establishing the First Bulgarian Empire'; the First Bulgarian Empire page: 'In 681, the Byzantines were compelled to…
741: Cliopatria adds Slavonia to the shape and removes the Macedonian exclave.
Summer 791: Charlemagne invades the khaganate.
October 791: the Franks withdraw.
796: Pippin of Italy takes Pannonia.
800: the central Hungarian plain returns to the Avars in Cliopatria.
804: Khan Krum's Bulgaria takes Transylvania.
805: the Avar Khaganate ends.

wars.name: Lombard-Gepid War
wars.outcome: The Avars and Lombards 'destroyed much of the Gepid kingdom' in 567; the Avars took the east and, after the Lombards left in 568, the rest.

wars.name: Avar siege and capture of Sirmium
Avar-Byzantine Balkan war of Maurice's reign
wars.outcome: Avar captures on the Danube (583, 586), a ransomed siege of Singidunum (588), Byzantine crossings under Priscus (593, 599) and Peter (594, 601); no lasting border change.

wars.name: Avar-Byzantine war of Heraclius' reign
wars.outcome: The Avars took Naissus and Serdica (615), besieged Thessalonica (617) and, with the Persians, besieged Constantinople from 29 June 626; the assaults of 6-7 August were repelled and they retreated.

wars.name: Samo's rebellion against the Avars
wars.outcome: Samo's 'string of victories over the Avars' made him king and split the western Slavs from the Avars; in 631 or 632 he also beat Dagobert I's Franks.

wars.name: Kubrat's revolt
wars.outcome: Kubrat united the Onogur Bulgars and 'overthrew Avar domination' between 630 and 635.

wars.name: Bulgar settlement on the lower Danube
wars.outcome: The Avar land 'was further reduced by the Bulgars around 680'; Byzantium recognised Bulgaria in 681.

wars.name: Charlemagne's Avar War
wars.outcome: Avar attacks on Bavaria and Italy failed in 788; Charlemagne reached the Raba in 791; Pippin of Italy and Eric of Friuli made the khagan submit in 796 and the Franks seized Pannonia; the Avars who refused withdrew east of the Tisza.

wars.name: Bulgarian conquest of the Avar east
wars.outcome: 'Between 804 and 806 the Bulgarian armies thoroughly eliminated the Avar Khaganate'; a border with the Frankish Empire was established along the middle Danube or the Tisza.
